label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. Despite advanced educational attainment, heavy digital engagement does not appear to buffer against psychological difficulties, and may coincide with social isolation and mental health challenges.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores indicating perceived social disconnection
Higher depressive symptom severity suggesting persistent low mood and functional impact
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most pronounced of the three distress indicators
Extended daily screen time exceeding 5 hours, potentially reflecting both occupational and leisure digital engagement
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety pointing to compounded emotional burden
tone: Concerned and empathetic, acknowledging significant psychological distress across multiple domains

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below typical thresholds, these individuals appear to be psychologically well-adjusted and emotionally stable. They spend a moderate amount of time (1–3 hours) on relevant activities, suggesting balanced engagement rather than excessive or minimal use.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness levels (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77)
Maintains moderate daily engagement of 1–3 hours
Demonstrates consistent emotional stability across all three psychological dimensions

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the emotional distress patterns typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping mechanisms that buffer against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting minimal clinical depression
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating limited generalized anxiety
Relatively modest daily screen/social media engagement (1–3 hours)
Possible disconnect between social isolation feelings and overall emotional well-being
tone: Quietly disconnected yet emotionally stable; introspective rather than distressed
